```cpp
TEST_CASE("RunHighlightJob: tokenizes the range and stamps version, epoch and grammar version", "[text-worker]")
{
    ScopeTable scopes;
    const GrammarSnapshot g = CompileTestGrammar(kBlockyGrammar, scopes, 5);
    const Rope rope = Rope::FromUtf8(Lines(40, "if \"a\" /* b"));
    MatchScratch scratch{ RegexLimits{} };
    const HighlightResult r = RunHighlightJob(MakeJob(rope, g, std::make_shared<StateTable>(), 0, 40), scratch, {});
    CHECK(r.version == 7u);
    CHECK(r.epoch == 1u);
    CHECK(r.grammarVersion == 5u);
    CHECK(r.firstRow == 0u);
    REQUIRE(r.rows.size() == 40u);
    const auto full = FullTokenize(rope, *g, 0);
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < 40; ++i) CHECK(RunsEqual(r.rows[i].tokens, full[i]));
    CHECK_FALSE(r.converged);
}

TEST_CASE("RunHighlightJob: the frame budget ends a slice between rows; slices concatenate to the full result", "[text-worker]")
{
    ScopeTable scopes;
    const GrammarSnapshot g = CompileTestGrammar(kBlockyGrammar, scopes);
    const Rope rope = Rope::FromUtf8(Lines(200, "x 1 \"s\""));
    auto states = std::make_shared<StateTable>();
    MatchScratch scratch{ RegexLimits{} };
    std::uint64_t now = 0;
    const std::function<std::uint64_t()> clock = [&now] { return now += 10; };
    std::vector<HighlightRowResult> all;
    std::uint32_t start = 0;
    StateId state = StateTable::kRoot;
    int slices = 0;
    while (start < 200 && slices < 100)
    {
        HighlightJob j = MakeJob(rope, g, states, start, 200, state);
        j.limits.highlightFrameBudgetUs = 300;
        HighlightResult r = RunHighlightJob(j, scratch, clock);
        REQUIRE_FALSE(r.rows.empty());
        CHECK(r.rows.size() < 200u);
        start += static_cast<std::uint32_t>(r.rows.size());
        state = r.rows.back().tokens.endState;
        for (auto& row : r.rows) all.push_back(std::move(row));
        ++slices;
    }
    CHECK(slices > 1);
    const auto full = FullTokenize(rope, *g, 0);
    REQUIRE(all.size() == 200u);
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < 200; ++i) CHECK(RunsEqual(all[i].tokens, full[i]));
}

{
    ScopeTable scopes;
    const GrammarSnapshot g = CompileTestGrammar(kBlockyGrammar, scopes);
    const Rope rope = Rope::FromUtf8(Lines(500, "if \"x\" 1"));
    {
        ThreadedHighlightExecutor exec;
        HighlightJob a = MakeJob(rope, g, std::make_shared<StateTable>(), 0, 500);
        HighlightJob b = MakeJob(rope, g, std::make_shared<StateTable>(), 100, 200);
        b.urgent = true;
        const auto qa = a.results, qb = b.results;
        exec.Submit(std::move(a));
        exec.Submit(std::move(b));
        exec.WaitIdle();
        const auto ra = qa->TakeAll(), rb = qb->TakeAll();
        REQUIRE(ra.size() == 1u);
        REQUIRE(rb.size() == 1u);
        CHECK(ra[0].rows.size() == 500u);
        CHECK(rb[0].firstRow == 100u);
    }
    {
        ThreadedHighlightExecutor exec;
        for (int i = 0; i < 20; ++i) exec.Submit(MakeJob(rope, g, std::make_shared<StateTable>(), 0, 500));
    }   // destructor: stop requested, pending jobs dropped, thread joined
    SUCCEED();
}

    CHECK(q->Empty());
    CHECK(exec.RunNext());
    CHECK(exec.Pending() == 0u);
    CHECK_FALSE(q->Empty());
    CHECK_FALSE(exec.RunNext());
}
```

`ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Syntax/HighlightWorker.hpp`:

```cpp
#pragma once

// The highlight worker (spec s4.4): tokenizing jobs over immutable
// RopeSnapshots, results handed to the UI thread through a queue. See the
// TE3-15 task text.

#include "TextEditor/Core/Rope.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/Grammar.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/StateTable.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/SyntaxLimits.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/SyntaxTypes.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/Tokenizer.hpp"

#include <condition_variable>
#include <cstdint>
#include <deque>
#include <functional>
#include <memory>
#include <mutex>
#include <optional>
#include <stop_token>
#include <thread>
#include <vector>

namespace Arcane::Text
{
    struct HighlightRowResult
    {
        StateId startState = StateTable::kRoot;
        LineTokens tokens;
    };

    struct HighlightResult
    {
        std::uint64_t ticket = 0;
        std::uint64_t epoch = 0;            // the cache session the StateIds belong to
        std::uint64_t version = 0;          // the snapshot's buffer version
        std::uint64_t grammarVersion = 0;
        std::uint32_t firstRow = 0;         // in version-`version` coordinates
        std::vector<HighlightRowResult> rows;
        bool converged = false;             // stopped because row firstRow + rows.size() starts in its known state
    };

    class HighlightResultQueue
    {
    public:
        void Push(HighlightResult result);
        [[nodiscard]] std::vector<HighlightResult> TakeAll();
        [[nodiscard]] bool Empty() const;

    private:
        mutable std::mutex m_mutex;
        std::vector<HighlightResult> m_results;
    };

    struct HighlightJob
    {
        std::uint64_t ticket = 0;
        std::uint64_t epoch = 0;
        RopeSnapshot snapshot;
        GrammarSnapshot grammar;                      // held: a reload cannot free it under the job
        std::shared_ptr<StateTable> states;           // the cache session's table, held likewise
        std::uint32_t startRow = 0;
        StateId startState = StateTable::kRoot;
        std::optional<LineTokens> resume;             // startRow's partial tokens to continue
        std::uint32_t endRow = 0;                     // exclusive
        std::vector<StateId> knownStarts;             // [i] = the cache's start state of row startRow + 1 + i, kNoState if none
        SyntaxLimits limits;
        ISyntaxProblemSink* problems = nullptr;
        bool urgent = false;                          // visible rows are waiting on it (s4.4)
        std::shared_ptr<HighlightResultQueue> results;
    };

    // One slice, on the calling thread, with that thread's scratch. Pure.
    [[nodiscard]] HighlightResult RunHighlightJob(const HighlightJob& job, MatchScratch& scratch,
                                                  const std::function<std::uint64_t()>& clock);

    class IHighlightExecutor
    {
    public:
        virtual ~IHighlightExecutor() = default;
        virtual void Submit(HighlightJob job) = 0;
    };

    class ThreadedHighlightExecutor final : public IHighlightExecutor
    {
    public:
        ThreadedHighlightExecutor();
        ~ThreadedHighlightExecutor() override;
        void Submit(HighlightJob job) override;
        void WaitIdle();
        [[nodiscard]] std::size_t Pending() const;

    private:
        void Loop(std::stop_token stop);

        mutable std::mutex m_mutex;
        std::condition_variable_any m_wake;
        std::condition_variable m_idle;
        std::deque<HighlightJob> m_jobs;
        bool m_running = false;
        std::jthread m_thread;   // last: starts after the members it uses exist, joins first
    };

    class ManualHighlightExecutor final : public IHighlightExecutor
    {
    public:
        explicit ManualHighlightExecutor(std::function<std::uint64_t()> clock = {}) : m_clock(std::move(clock)) {}
        void Submit(HighlightJob job) override { m_jobs.push_back(std::move(job)); }
        [[nodiscard]] std::size_t Pending() const noexcept { return m_jobs.size(); }
        [[nodiscard]] const HighlightJob& Job(std::size_t i) const { return m_jobs[i]; }
        bool RunNext();
        std::size_t RunAll();

    private:
        std::deque<HighlightJob> m_jobs;
        MatchScratch m_scratch{ RegexLimits{} };   // the "worker thread's" scratch, distinct from the UI's
        std::function<std::uint64_t()> m_clock;
    };
}
```

`ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Syntax/HighlightWorker.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/HighlightWorker.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <string>

namespace Arcane::Text
{
    void HighlightResultQueue::Push(HighlightResult result)
    {
        std::lock_guard lock(m_mutex);
        m_results.push_back(std::move(result));
    }

    std::vector<HighlightResult> HighlightResultQueue::TakeAll()
    {
        std::lock_guard lock(m_mutex);
        std::vector<HighlightResult> out;
        out.swap(m_results);
        return out;
    }

    bool HighlightResultQueue::Empty() const
    {
        std::lock_guard lock(m_mutex);
        return m_results.empty();
    }

    HighlightResult RunHighlightJob(const HighlightJob& job, MatchScratch& scratch, const std::function<std::uint64_t()>& clock)
    {
        scratch.SetLimits(job.limits.regex);
        HighlightResult out;
        out.ticket = job.ticket;
        out.epoch = job.epoch;
        out.version = job.snapshot.version;
        out.grammarVersion = job.grammar->grammarVersion();
        out.firstRow = job.startRow;
        const Rope& rope = job.snapshot.rope;
        const std::uint32_t endRow = std::min(job.endRow, rope.LineCount());
        Tokenizer tokenizer(*job.grammar, *job.states, scratch);
        TokenizeOptions opt;
        opt.longLineMaxBytes = job.limits.longLineMaxBytes;
        opt.lineBudgetUs = job.limits.tokenizeLineBudgetUs;
        opt.clock = clock ? &clock : nullptr;
        opt.problems = job.problems;
        const auto now = [&clock] { return clock ? clock() : SteadyNowUs(); };
        const std::uint64_t t0 = now();
        const auto overBudget = [&] { return job.limits.highlightFrameBudgetUs != 0 && now() - t0 >= job.limits.highlightFrameBudgetUs; };
        std::string line;
        StateId state = job.startState;
        for (std::uint32_t row = job.startRow; row < endRow; ++row)
        {
            if (row > job.startRow)
            {
                const std::size_t k = row - job.startRow - 1;
                if (k < job.knownStarts.size() && job.knownStarts[k] == state)
                {
                    out.converged = true;   // the cache already holds everything from here (s4.4)
                    break;
                }
                if (overBudget()) break;
            }
            CopyRowForTokenize(rope, row, job.limits.longLineMaxBytes, line);
            HighlightRowResult r;
            r.startState = state;
            if (row == job.startRow && job.resume)
            {
                r.tokens = *job.resume;
                tokenizer.ResumeLine(line, r.tokens, opt);
            }
            else
            {
                r.tokens = tokenizer.TokenizeLine(line, state, opt);
            }
            while (r.tokens.partial && !overBudget()) tokenizer.ResumeLine(line, r.tokens, opt);
            const bool partial = r.tokens.partial;
            state = r.tokens.endState;
            out.rows.push_back(std::move(r));
            if (partial) break;   // the next job resumes this row
        }
        return out;
    }

    ThreadedHighlightExecutor::ThreadedHighlightExecutor()
        : m_thread([this](std::stop_token stop) { Loop(stop); })
    {
    }

    ThreadedHighlightExecutor::~ThreadedHighlightExecutor()
    {
        m_thread.request_stop();
        m_wake.notify_all();
    }

    void ThreadedHighlightExecutor::Submit(HighlightJob job)
    {
        {
            std::lock_guard lock(m_mutex);
            if (job.urgent) m_jobs.push_front(std::move(job));
            else m_jobs.push_back(std::move(job));
        }
        m_wake.notify_one();
    }

    void ThreadedHighlightExecutor::WaitIdle()
    {
        std::unique_lock lock(m_mutex);
        m_idle.wait(lock, [this] { return m_jobs.empty() && !m_running; });
    }

    std::size_t ThreadedHighlightExecutor::Pending() const
    {
        std::lock_guard lock(m_mutex);
        return m_jobs.size();
    }

    void ThreadedHighlightExecutor::Loop(std::stop_token stop)
    {
        MatchScratch scratch{ RegexLimits{} };   // this thread's PCRE2 state; nothing mutable is shared (s4.2)
        const std::function<std::uint64_t()> clock;
        for (;;)
        {
            HighlightJob job;
            {
                std::unique_lock lock(m_mutex);
                m_wake.wait(lock, stop, [this] { return !m_jobs.empty(); });
                if (stop.stop_requested()) return;   // queued jobs are dropped: each owns its result queue, nothing waits on them
                job = std::move(m_jobs.front());
                m_jobs.pop_front();
                m_running = true;
            }
            HighlightResult result = RunHighlightJob(job, scratch, clock);
            job.results->Push(std::move(result));
            {
                std::lock_guard lock(m_mutex);
                m_running = false;
            }
            m_idle.notify_all();
        }
    }

    bool ManualHighlightExecutor::RunNext()
    {
        if (m_jobs.empty()) return false;
        HighlightJob job = std::move(m_jobs.front());
        m_jobs.pop_front();
        job.results->Push(RunHighlightJob(job, m_scratch, m_clock));
        return true;
    }

    std::size_t ManualHighlightExecutor::RunAll()
    {
        std::size_t n = 0;
        while (RunNext()) ++n;
        return n;
    }
}
```

`condition_variable_any::wait(lock, stop_token, pred)` also returns when stop is requested; checking `stop_requested()` after it (rather than the predicate's result) means shutdown never drains the queue -- a job already running finishes, every queued one is dropped, and the `jthread` joins promptly (the destructor test submits 20 jobs).

### Task TE3-16: Worker results mapped forward through the edit log; priority toward the view (spec s4.4, s11.2)

**Files:**
- Modify: `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Syntax/HighlightCache.hpp` (members, `DrainResults`, `ApplyResult`, `Schedule`), `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Syntax/HighlightCache.cpp` (`BeginFrame` replaced; three new functions)
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/HighlightVersionTest.cpp`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: TE3-14 `HighlightCache`, `MapRowForward`; TE3-15 `HighlightJob`, `HighlightResult`, `HighlightResultQueue`, `IHighlightExecutor`, `ManualHighlightExecutor`, `ThreadedHighlightExecutor`
- Produces: the finished `HighlightCache` (no new public API)

Version discipline (spec s4.4, s11.2): a result produced at version *v* arrives at the current version *c*. Results from another epoch or grammar version are discarded on sight. Otherwise every result row is mapped through `EditsSince(v)`: a row inside an edited range is dropped (edited rows are always re-tokenized by the normal frontier work); every other row is stored at its shifted position -- but only at or below the frontier (ready rows are never overwritten), and every contiguous stored block gets a checkpoint at its first row and at the row after it. So the rows **above the earliest edit** chain from the frontier and become ready by integer compares, and the rows **below** become ready only when the re-tokenized edited rows **converge** into the start state they were produced with; if not, the compare fails at that row and the normal work re-tokenizes from there. Nothing from an older version can become ready without passing that compare. Scheduling: one job in flight per cache; each frame without one, the cache submits a slice from the frontier toward the visible end plus a visible-height margin (and nothing when the frontier is already past it -- "only as far as the view has been"), with the next `max(syncCatchUpLines, 2 x last slice's rows)` known start states for the worker's convergence stop; a frame in which `Line()` refused a visible row makes the next job **urgent**.

```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "Helpers/TextGrammarFixtures.hpp"
#include "Helpers/TextHighlightFixtures.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/HighlightCache.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/HighlightWorker.hpp"

#include <chrono>

using namespace Arcane::Text;
using namespace Arcane::Test;

namespace
{
    std::string Lines(std::uint32_t n, std::string_view line)
    {
        std::string s;
        for (std::uint32_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) { s += line; if (i + 1 < n) s += '\n'; }
        return s;
    }

    struct Env
    {
        ScopeTable scopes;
        GrammarSnapshot grammar = CompileTestGrammar(kBlockyGrammar, scopes);
        MatchScratch ui{ RegexLimits{} };
        HighlightCache::Services Services(IHighlightExecutor* exec)
        {
            HighlightCache::Services s;
            s.uiScratch = &ui;
            s.executor = exec;
            return s;
        }
    };

    SyntaxLimits WorkerOnly()
    {
        SyntaxLimits l;
        l.syncCatchUpLines = 0;   // the UI never tokenizes: every row comes from the worker
        return l;
    }
}

TEST_CASE("Version discipline: rows above the earliest edit since the job's version are applied", "[text-highlight][text-worker]")
{
    Env e;
    ManualHighlightExecutor exec;
    FakeHighlightText text(Lines(300, "n = 1"));
    HighlightCache cache(text, e.grammar, e.Services(&exec), WorkerOnly());
    cache.BeginFrame(0, 49);
    REQUIRE(exec.Pending() == 1u);
    CHECK(exec.Job(0).endRow == 100u);                     // visible end + a visible-height margin
    text.Insert(text.RowStart(60) + 4, "2");               // edit row 60 while the job is held
    exec.RunNext();                                        // the job ran on the version before the edit
    cache.BeginFrame(0, 49);
    CHECK(cache.Stats().resultsApplied == 1u);
    CHECK(cache.Frontier() == 60u);                        // 0..59 applied; 60 is edited; 61.. wait behind it
    CHECK(cache.Peek(59) != nullptr);
    CHECK(cache.Peek(61) == nullptr);
    CHECK(ReadyRowsMatchFull(cache, text, *e.grammar, 0));
    REQUIRE(exec.Pending() == 1u);
    CHECK(exec.Job(0).startRow == 60u);
    exec.RunNext();
    cache.BeginFrame(0, 49);
    CHECK(cache.Frontier() >= 100u);                       // row 60 converged: 61..99 became ready by compares
    CHECK(ReadyRowsMatchFull(cache, text, *e.grammar, 0));
}

TEST_CASE("Version discipline: rows below an edit are applied shifted only when the edit converged", "[text-highlight][text-worker]")
{
    Env e;
    ManualHighlightExecutor exec;
    FakeHighlightText text(Lines(300, "n = 1"));
    HighlightCache cache(text, e.grammar, e.Services(&exec), WorkerOnly());
    cache.BeginFrame(0, 99);                               // job: rows 0..199
    text.Insert(text.RowEnd(30), "\nif 2\nelse 3");        // +2 rows after row 30: converging
    exec.RunNext();
    cache.BeginFrame(0, 99);
    CHECK(cache.Frontier() == 30u);
    REQUIRE(exec.Pending() == 1u);
    exec.RunNext();                                        // re-tokenizes 30..32, converges at 33
    cache.BeginFrame(0, 99);
    CHECK(cache.Frontier() >= 202u);                       // the shifted rows 33..201 were kept
    CHECK(ReadyRowsMatchFull(cache, text, *e.grammar, 0));

    // A non-converging edit: open a comment at row 10 while a job is held.
    cache.BeginFrame(0, 299);
    while (exec.Pending()) { exec.RunNext(); cache.BeginFrame(0, 299); }
    REQUIRE(cache.Frontier() == cache.RowCount());
    text.Insert(text.RowStart(10), "/*");
    cache.BeginFrame(0, 299);
    exec.RunAll();
    cache.BeginFrame(0, 299);
    CHECK(ReadyRowsMatchFull(cache, text, *e.grammar, 0));   // never stale, at every step
    for (int i = 0; i < 10 && cache.Frontier() < cache.RowCount(); ++i) { exec.RunAll(); cache.BeginFrame(0, 299); }
    CHECK(cache.Frontier() == cache.RowCount());
    CHECK(ReadyRowsMatchFull(cache, text, *e.grammar, 0));
}

TEST_CASE("No starvation: Follow appending every frame still colours every row above", "[text-highlight][text-worker]")
{
    Env e;
    std::uint64_t now = 0;
    ManualHighlightExecutor exec([&now] { return now += 10; });   // 10 us per clock read
    FakeHighlightText text(Lines(2000, "x 1 \"s\""));
    SyntaxLimits l = WorkerOnly();
    l.highlightFrameBudgetUs = 500;                              // ~50 rows per slice
    HighlightCache cache(text, e.grammar, e.Services(&exec), l);
    int frames = 0;
    for (; frames < 100 && cache.Frontier() + 2 < cache.RowCount(); ++frames)
    {
        text.Append("\ntick 1");                                  // the log grows every frame
        const std::uint32_t last = text.Rows() - 1;
        cache.BeginFrame(last > 40 ? last - 40 : 0, last);
        exec.RunNext();                                           // the slice runs on this frame's version...
    }                                                             // ...and lands next frame, one append later
    CHECK(frames < 60);                                           // ~40 slices of 50 rows + slack
    CHECK(cache.Frontier() + 2 >= cache.RowCount());
    CHECK(ReadyRowsMatchFull(cache, text, *e.grammar, 0));
}

}

    const GrammarSnapshot v2 = CompileTestGrammar(R"({"format":"arcsyntax","version":1,"name":"Blocky","scope":"source.blocky",
        "patterns":[{"match":"[0-9]+","scope":"constant.numeric.v2"}]})", e.scopes, 2);
    cache.SetGrammar(v2);
    e.grammar.reset();                                    // only the held job keeps v1 alive now
    exec.RunNext();                                       // runs on v1 without touching freed memory
    cache.BeginFrame(0, 49);
    CHECK(cache.Stats().resultsDiscarded == 1u);
    CHECK(cache.Peek(0) == nullptr);
    exec.RunAll();
    cache.BeginFrame(0, 49);
    REQUIRE(cache.Peek(0) != nullptr);
    CHECK(DescribeRuns(*cache.Peek(0), e.scopes) == "0: 3:constant.numeric.v2");
}
```

and add:

```cpp
    void HighlightCache::DrainResults()
    {
        for (HighlightResult& r : m_results->TakeAll())
        {
            if (r.ticket == m_ticket) m_inFlight = false;
            ApplyResult(r);
        }
    }

    void HighlightCache::ApplyResult(HighlightResult& result)
    {
        if (m_mode != Mode::Stateful || !m_grammar || result.epoch != m_epoch ||
            result.grammarVersion != m_grammar->grammarVersion() || result.version > m_syncedVersion)
        {
            ++m_stats.resultsDiscarded;   // another session, another grammar: its StateIds mean nothing here
            return;
        }
        std::span<const EditLogEntry> edits;
        if (result.version < m_syncedVersion)
        {
            edits = m_text.EditsSince(result.version);
            if (!m_text.EditLogCovers(result.version) || edits.empty() || edits.front().version != result.version + 1)
            {
                ++m_stats.resultsDiscarded;   // the log no longer reaches back to the result's version
                return;
            }
        }
        if (!result.rows.empty()) m_lastJobRows = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(result.rows.size());
        std::optional<std::uint32_t> last;   // last stored row of the current contiguous block
        const auto closeBlock = [&] {
            if (last && *last + 1 < m_rows.size()) AddCheckpoint(*last + 1);   // the row after a block is verified against it
            last.reset();
        };
        std::uint64_t stored = 0;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < result.rows.size(); ++i)
        {
            const std::optional<std::uint32_t> mapped = MapRowForward(result.firstRow + static_cast<std::uint32_t>(i), edits);
            if (!mapped || *mapped >= m_rows.size() || *mapped < Frontier())
            {
                closeBlock();   // edited since (re-tokenized by the frontier work), gone, or already ready
                continue;
            }
            const std::uint32_t row = *mapped;
            if (!last || row != *last + 1 || m_rows[*last].tokens.partial)
            {
                closeBlock();
                AddCheckpoint(row);   // a block's first row is verified against the row above it
            }
            HighlightRow& dst = m_rows[row];
            dst.hasTokens = true;
            dst.startState = result.rows[i].startState;
            dst.tokens = std::move(result.rows[i].tokens);
            last = row;
            ++stored;
        }
        closeBlock();
        ++m_stats.resultsApplied;
        m_stats.rowsFromWorker += stored;
        if (stored) ++m_contentGeneration;
        ResolveFree();
    }

    void HighlightCache::Schedule()
    {
        if (!m_services.executor || m_inFlight || !m_grammar) return;
        const auto rows = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(m_rows.size());
        const std::uint32_t visible = m_lastVisible - m_firstVisible + 1;
        const auto target = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::min<std::uint64_t>(rows, static_cast<std::uint64_t>(m_lastVisible) + 1 + visible));
        std::uint32_t start = Frontier();
        if (start >= target) return;   // only as far as the view has been (s4.4)
        HighlightJob job;
        if (start > 0 && m_rows[start - 1].tokens.partial)
        {
            --start;
            job.resume = m_rows[start].tokens;
            job.startState = m_rows[start].startState;
        }
        else
        {
            job.startState = start == 0 ? StateTable::kRoot : m_rows[start - 1].tokens.endState;
        }
        job.ticket = ++m_ticket;
        job.epoch = m_epoch;
        job.snapshot = m_snapshot;
        job.grammar = m_grammar;
        job.states = m_states;
        job.startRow = start;
        job.endRow = target;
        const std::uint32_t window = std::max(m_limits.syncCatchUpLines, 2 * m_lastJobRows);
        const auto knownEnd = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::min<std::uint64_t>(target, static_cast<std::uint64_t>(start) + 1 + window));
        for (std::uint32_t r = start + 1; r < knownEnd; ++r)
            job.knownStarts.push_back(m_rows[r].hasTokens ? m_rows[r].startState : kNoState);
        job.limits = m_limits;
        job.problems = m_services.problems;
        job.urgent = m_urgentLastFrame;
        job.results = m_results;
        m_inFlight = true;
        ++m_stats.jobsSubmitted;
        m_services.executor->Submit(std::move(job));
    }
```

`Reset()` does not clear `m_inFlight`: the job of the previous epoch still holds the slot until its (discarded) result is drained, so at most one job per cache is ever queued.

```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>
#include <rapidcheck.h>
#include <rapidcheck/catch.h>

#include "Helpers/TextGrammarFixtures.hpp"
#include "Helpers/TextHighlightFixtures.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/HighlightCache.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/HighlightWorker.hpp"

using namespace Arcane::Text;
using namespace Arcane::Test;

namespace
{
    const std::vector<std::string>& Pieces()
    {
        static const std::vector<std::string> p = { "a", "if ", "12", "\"", "\\\"", "/*", "*/", "//", " ", "\n", "\n",
                                                    "{", "}", "fn x", "else", "\"k\": ", std::string(30, 'q') };
        return p;
    }

    std::string RandomText(std::size_t maxPieces)
    {
        const auto picks = *rc::gen::container<std::vector<std::size_t>>(rc::gen::inRange<std::size_t>(0, Pieces().size()));
        std::string s;
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < picks.size() && i < maxPieces; ++i) s += Pieces()[picks[i]];
        return s;
    }
}

TEST_CASE("Highlight property: after random edits, held/stale worker slices and partial catch-up, every row equals a full re-tokenize",
          "[text-highlight][property]")
{
    rc::prop("incremental == full", [] {
        ScopeTable scopes;
        const GrammarSnapshot g = CompileTestGrammar(kBlockyGrammar, scopes);
        MatchScratch ui{ RegexLimits{} };
        ManualHighlightExecutor exec;
        FakeHighlightText text(RandomText(80));
        SyntaxLimits l;
        l.longLineMaxBytes = 24;   // many generated lines exceed it: the cap and root resync are under test too
        l.syncCatchUpLines = *rc::gen::inRange<std::uint32_t>(0, 6);
        HighlightCache::Services s;
        s.uiScratch = &ui;
        s.executor = &exec;
        HighlightCache cache(text, g, s, l);

        const int steps = *rc::gen::inRange(1, 30);
        for (int step = 0; step < steps; ++step)
        {
            switch (*rc::gen::inRange(0, 4))
            {
                case 0:   // an edit
                {
                    const std::string current = text.Text();
                    const std::size_t a = *rc::gen::inRange<std::size_t>(0, current.size() + 1);
                    const std::size_t b = std::min(current.size(), a + *rc::gen::inRange<std::size_t>(0, 12));
                    text.Replace({ a, b }, RandomText(4));
                    break;
                }
                case 1:   // a frame, drawing a random visible window
                {
                    const std::uint32_t rows = text.Rows();
                    const std::uint32_t first = *rc::gen::inRange<std::uint32_t>(0, rows);
                    const std::uint32_t last = std::min(rows - 1, first + *rc::gen::inRange<std::uint32_t>(0, 10));
                    cache.BeginFrame(first, last);
                    for (std::uint32_t r = first; r <= last; ++r) (void)cache.Line(r);
                    break;
                }
                case 2:   // the held worker runs (possibly on a stale version)
                    exec.RunNext();
                    break;
                case 3:   // a frame without drawing
                    cache.BeginFrame(0, 0);
                    break;
            }
            if (cache.SyncedVersion() == text.Version())   // comparable only once the cache has seen the edits
                RC_ASSERT(ReadyRowsMatchFull(cache, text, *g, l.longLineMaxBytes));   // never stale
        }

        // Drive to completion and compare every row.
        for (int i = 0; i < 50 && cache.Frontier() < cache.RowCount(); ++i)
        {
            cache.BeginFrame(0, text.Rows() - 1);
            exec.RunAll();
        }
        cache.BeginFrame(0, text.Rows() - 1);
        RC_ASSERT(cache.Frontier() == cache.RowCount());
        const auto full = FullTokenize(text.Snapshot().rope, *g, l.longLineMaxBytes);
        for (std::uint32_t r = 0; r < cache.RowCount(); ++r)
        {
            const LineTokens* t = cache.Peek(r);
            RC_ASSERT(t != nullptr);
            RC_ASSERT(RunsEqual(*t, full[r]));
        }
    });
}
```

### Task TE3-18: Brackets from the grammar, skipping string and comment scopes (spec s4.6)

**Files:**
- Create: `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Syntax/Brackets.hpp`, `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Syntax/Brackets.cpp`
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/BracketsTest.cpp`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `Rope` (`OffsetToPoint`, `LineStart`, `LineEnd`, `LineCount`, `CopyTo`); `GrammarRules::Brackets()` (TE3-8); `TokenRun::flags`, `kRunString`, `kRunComment` (TE3-4)
- Produces (namespace `Arcane::Text`):
  - `using TokenLookup = std::function<const LineTokens*(std::uint32_t row)>;` (pass `HighlightCache::Peek` -- never a catch-up)
  - `struct BracketPair { ByteOffset open; ByteOffset close; }`
  - `bool IsCodeAt(const LineTokens* tokens, std::uint32_t col) noexcept`
  - `std::optional<ByteOffset> FindMatchingBracket(const Rope&, ByteOffset at, const GrammarRules&, const TokenLookup&, std::uint32_t maxLines, std::uint32_t maxLineBytes)`
  - `std::optional<BracketPair> FindEnclosingBrackets(const Rope&, ByteOffset cursor, const GrammarRules&, const TokenLookup&, std::uint32_t maxLines, std::uint32_t maxLineBytes)`

Pairs come from the grammar's `brackets`; a bracket byte whose run carries `kRunString` or `kRunComment` is not a bracket (s4.6). A row whose tokens are not ready (`nullptr`) is treated as code -- matching never waits for, or triggers, tokenizing. The search covers at most `maxLines` rows each way (`editor.text.bracketScanMaxLines`) and at most `maxLineBytes` of any line (`editor.text.longLineMaxBytes`: past the cap a line is plain text, so it has no brackets either). TE4 draws the primary cursor's enclosing pair when the selection is empty (Zed's rule, s4.6) and binds go-to-matching-bracket; TE5's `%` uses `FindMatchingBracket`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test** -- `ArcaneTests/src/Text/BracketsTest.cpp`:

```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include "Helpers/TextGrammarFixtures.hpp"
#include "Helpers/TextHighlightFixtures.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/Brackets.hpp"

using namespace Arcane::Text;
using namespace Arcane::Test;

namespace
{
    struct Doc
    {
        ScopeTable scopes;
        GrammarSnapshot g = CompileTestGrammar(kBlockyGrammar, scopes);
        Rope rope;
        std::vector<LineTokens> tokens;
        explicit Doc(std::string_view text) : rope(Rope::FromUtf8(text)), tokens(FullTokenize(rope, *g, 0)) {}
        TokenLookup Lookup() const
        {
            return [this](std::uint32_t row) -> const LineTokens* { return row < tokens.size() ? &tokens[row] : nullptr; };
        }
        ByteOffset At(std::string_view needle, std::size_t nth = 1) const
        {
            const std::string s = rope.ToString();
            std::size_t p = std::string::npos;
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < nth; ++i) p = s.find(needle, p == std::string::npos ? 0 : p + 1);
            REQUIRE(p != std::string::npos);
            return p;
        }
    };
}

TEST_CASE("Brackets: the match skips brackets inside strings and comments", "[text-brackets]")
{
    Doc d(R"(fn f(a, "(", b) { x(1) /* } */ })");
    const auto close = FindMatchingBracket(d.rope, d.At("("), d.g->Rules(), d.Lookup(), 100, 0);
    REQUIRE(close.has_value());
    CHECK(*close == d.At(")", 2));                     // not the "(" in the string
    const auto brace = FindMatchingBracket(d.rope, d.At("{"), d.g->Rules(), d.Lookup(), 100, 0);
    REQUIRE(brace.has_value());
    CHECK(*brace == d.At("}", 2));                     // not the } in the comment
    CHECK(FindMatchingBracket(d.rope, *brace, d.g->Rules(), d.Lookup(), 100, 0) == d.At("{"));   // backwards too
    CHECK_FALSE(FindMatchingBracket(d.rope, d.At("(", 2), d.g->Rules(), d.Lookup(), 100, 0).has_value());   // in a string
    CHECK_FALSE(FindMatchingBracket(d.rope, d.At("a"), d.g->Rules(), d.Lookup(), 100, 0).has_value());     // not a bracket
}

TEST_CASE("Brackets: the enclosing pair of a cursor, across lines", "[text-brackets]")
{
    Doc d("fn f() {\n  x(1, 2)\n  y\n}");
    const auto inner = FindEnclosingBrackets(d.rope, d.At("1"), d.g->Rules(), d.Lookup(), 100, 0);
    REQUIRE(inner.has_value());
    CHECK(inner->open == d.At("(", 2));
    CHECK(inner->close == d.At(")", 2));
    const auto outer = FindEnclosingBrackets(d.rope, d.At("y"), d.g->Rules(), d.Lookup(), 100, 0);
    REQUIRE(outer.has_value());
    CHECK(outer->open == d.At("{"));
    CHECK(outer->close == d.At("}"));
    CHECK_FALSE(FindEnclosingBrackets(d.rope, d.At("fn"), d.g->Rules(), d.Lookup(), 100, 0).has_value());
    CHECK_FALSE(FindEnclosingBrackets(d.rope, d.At("(") + 2, d.g->Rules(), d.Lookup(), 100, 0).has_value());   // after "()"
}

TEST_CASE("Brackets: maxLines and maxLineBytes bound the search", "[text-brackets]")
{
    std::string text = "{\n";
    for (int i = 0; i < 10; ++i) text += "a\n";
    text += "}";
    Doc d(text);
    CHECK_FALSE(FindMatchingBracket(d.rope, d.At("{"), d.g->Rules(), d.Lookup(), 5, 0).has_value());
    CHECK(FindMatchingBracket(d.rope, d.At("{"), d.g->Rules(), d.Lookup(), 20, 0) == d.At("}"));
    Doc wide("(" + std::string(100, 'a') + ")");
    CHECK_FALSE(FindMatchingBracket(wide.rope, 0, wide.g->Rules(), wide.Lookup(), 5, 50).has_value());   // ')' is past the cap
    CHECK(FindMatchingBracket(wide.rope, 0, wide.g->Rules(), wide.Lookup(), 5, 0) == 101u);
}

TEST_CASE("Brackets: rows without tokens are treated as code", "[text-brackets]")
{
    Doc d(R"(f("(") ))");
    const TokenLookup none = [](std::uint32_t) -> const LineTokens* { return nullptr; };
    CHECK(FindMatchingBracket(d.rope, d.At("("), d.g->Rules(), none, 10, 0) == d.At(")"));   // the string's ( now counts
    CHECK(IsCodeAt(nullptr, 3));
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

`ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Syntax/Brackets.hpp`:

```cpp
#pragma once

// Bracket pairs from the grammar (spec s4.6), skipping brackets in string.*
// and comment.* scopes. Pure; reads tokens only through TokenLookup.

#include "TextEditor/Core/Rope.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/Grammar.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/SyntaxTypes.hpp"

#include <cstdint>
#include <functional>
#include <optional>

namespace Arcane::Text
{
    using TokenLookup = std::function<const LineTokens*(std::uint32_t row)>;

    struct BracketPair
    {
        ByteOffset open = 0;
        ByteOffset close = 0;
        bool operator==(const BracketPair&) const = default;
    };

    // True when byte `col` of a line with `tokens` is code (not string or
    // comment). nullptr tokens = not highlighted yet = code.
    [[nodiscard]] bool IsCodeAt(const LineTokens* tokens, std::uint32_t col) noexcept;

    // `at` is a bracket's offset; returns its partner's offset.
    [[nodiscard]] std::optional<ByteOffset> FindMatchingBracket(const Rope& text, ByteOffset at, const GrammarRules& grammar,
                                                                const TokenLookup& tokens, std::uint32_t maxLines,
                                                                std::uint32_t maxLineBytes);
    // The innermost pair whose open is before `cursor` and close at or after it.
    [[nodiscard]] std::optional<BracketPair> FindEnclosingBrackets(const Rope& text, ByteOffset cursor, const GrammarRules& grammar,
                                                                   const TokenLookup& tokens, std::uint32_t maxLines,
                                                                   std::uint32_t maxLineBytes);
}
```

`ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Syntax/Brackets.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/Brackets.hpp"

#include <algorithm>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace Arcane::Text
{
    namespace
    {
        // One row's text, at most maxLineBytes of it (0 = all).
        void LoadRow(const Rope& text, std::uint32_t row, std::uint32_t maxLineBytes, std::string& out)
        {
            out.clear();
            const ByteOffset begin = text.LineStart(row);
            ByteOffset end = text.LineEnd(row);
            if (maxLineBytes != 0 && end - begin > maxLineBytes) end = begin + maxLineBytes;
            text.CopyTo(ByteRange{ begin, end }, out);
        }

        int PairOf(const GrammarRules& g, char c, bool& isOpen)
        {
            const auto& pairs = g.Brackets();
            for (std::size_t i = 0; i < pairs.size(); ++i)
            {
                if (pairs[i].first == c) { isOpen = true; return static_cast<int>(i); }
                if (pairs[i].second == c) { isOpen = false; return static_cast<int>(i); }
            }
            return -1;
        }
    }

    bool IsCodeAt(const LineTokens* tokens, std::uint32_t col) noexcept
    {
        if (!tokens || tokens->runs.empty()) return true;
        const auto it = std::upper_bound(tokens->runs.begin(), tokens->runs.end(), col,
                                         [](std::uint32_t c, const TokenRun& r) { return c < r.byteStart; });
        if (it == tokens->runs.begin()) return true;
        return (std::prev(it)->flags & (kRunString | kRunComment)) == 0;
    }

    std::optional<ByteOffset> FindMatchingBracket(const Rope& text, ByteOffset at, const GrammarRules& grammar,
                                                  const TokenLookup& tokens, std::uint32_t maxLines, std::uint32_t maxLineBytes)
    {
        if (at >= text.Size()) return std::nullopt;
        const Point p = text.OffsetToPoint(at);
        std::string line;
        LoadRow(text, p.row, maxLineBytes, line);
        if (p.col >= line.size()) return std::nullopt;
        bool isOpen = false;
        const int pair = PairOf(grammar, line[p.col], isOpen);
        if (pair < 0 || !IsCodeAt(tokens(p.row), p.col)) return std::nullopt;
        const char open = grammar.Brackets()[static_cast<std::size_t>(pair)].first;
        const char close = grammar.Brackets()[static_cast<std::size_t>(pair)].second;
        const std::uint32_t lastRow = text.LineCount() - 1;
        int depth = 0;
        if (isOpen)
        {
            const std::uint32_t stop = maxLines == 0 ? lastRow : static_cast<std::uint32_t>(std::min<std::uint64_t>(lastRow, std::uint64_t{ p.row } + maxLines));
            for (std::uint32_t row = p.row; row <= stop; ++row)
            {
                if (row != p.row) LoadRow(text, row, maxLineBytes, line);
                const LineTokens* t = tokens(row);
                for (std::size_t i = row == p.row ? p.col + 1 : 0; i < line.size(); ++i)
                {
                    if (line[i] != open && line[i] != close) continue;
                    if (!IsCodeAt(t, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(i))) continue;
                    if (line[i] == open) ++depth;
                    else if (depth == 0) return text.LineStart(row) + i;
                    else --depth;
                }
            }
            return std::nullopt;
        }
        const std::uint32_t stop = maxLines == 0 || p.row < maxLines ? 0 : p.row - maxLines;
        for (std::uint32_t row = p.row + 1; row-- > stop;)
        {
            if (row != p.row) LoadRow(text, row, maxLineBytes, line);
            const LineTokens* t = tokens(row);
            for (std::size_t i = row == p.row ? p.col : line.size(); i-- > 0;)
            {
                if (line[i] != open && line[i] != close) continue;
                if (!IsCodeAt(t, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(i))) continue;
                if (line[i] == close) ++depth;
                else if (depth == 0) return text.LineStart(row) + i;
                else --depth;
            }
        }
        return std::nullopt;
    }

    std::optional<BracketPair> FindEnclosingBrackets(const Rope& text, ByteOffset cursor, const GrammarRules& grammar,
                                                     const TokenLookup& tokens, std::uint32_t maxLines, std::uint32_t maxLineBytes)
    {
        if (grammar.Brackets().empty() || cursor == 0) return std::nullopt;
        const Point p = text.OffsetToPoint(std::min<ByteOffset>(cursor, text.Size()));
        std::vector<int> depth(grammar.Brackets().size(), 0);
        std::string line;
        const std::uint32_t stop = maxLines == 0 || p.row < maxLines ? 0 : p.row - maxLines;
        for (std::uint32_t row = p.row + 1; row-- > stop;)
        {
            LoadRow(text, row, maxLineBytes, line);
            const LineTokens* t = tokens(row);
            const std::size_t from = row == p.row ? std::min<std::size_t>(p.col, line.size()) : line.size();
            for (std::size_t i = from; i-- > 0;)
            {
                bool isOpen = false;
                const int pair = PairOf(grammar, line[i], isOpen);
                if (pair < 0 || !IsCodeAt(t, static_cast<std::uint32_t>(i))) continue;
                int& d = depth[static_cast<std::size_t>(pair)];
                if (!isOpen) { ++d; continue; }
                if (d > 0) { --d; continue; }
                const ByteOffset open = text.LineStart(row) + i;
                if (const auto close = FindMatchingBracket(text, open, grammar, tokens, maxLines, maxLineBytes); close && *close >= cursor)
                    return BracketPair{ open, *close };
                // unmatched (or closing before the cursor in unbalanced text): keep looking outward
            }
        }
        return std::nullopt;
    }
}
```

### Task TE3-19: Fold markers into FoldModel (spec s4.6)

**Files:**
- Create: `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Syntax/FoldMarkers.hpp`, `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Syntax/FoldMarkers.cpp`
- Modify: `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Core/FoldModel.hpp`, `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Core/FoldModel.cpp` (TE1's files: `MarkerFold`, `SetMarkerFolds`, `MarkerFolds`, `MarkerFoldEnd`, and the member `FoldableAt` -- marker region first, then TE1's `IndentRegionAt`)
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/FoldMarkersTest.cpp`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: TE1 `FoldModel` (default-constructed; `FoldRange { headerRow, lastRow }`; `static IndentRegionAt(const Rope&, row, tabSize) -> std::optional<FoldRange>`); `TextBuffer(Rope)` (tests); `LineTokens::foldMarker` (TE3-4/11); `HighlightCache::Peek`, `ContentGeneration`, `RowCount`, `Grammar` (TE3-14); `TokenLookup` (TE3-18)
- Produces (CANON A5; TE3-19 owns these):
  - `struct Arcane::Text::MarkerFold { std::uint32_t beginRow; std::uint32_t endRow; }` (Core)
  - `void FoldModel::SetMarkerFolds(std::vector<MarkerFold>)`, `std::span<const MarkerFold> FoldModel::MarkerFolds() const`, `std::optional<std::uint32_t> FoldModel::MarkerFoldEnd(std::uint32_t row) const` (public) (Core)
  - `std::optional<FoldRange> FoldModel::FoldableAt(const Rope& text, std::uint32_t row, std::uint32_t tabSize) const` -- the one "is this row foldable" query: the marker region `FoldRange{ row, *MarkerFoldEnd(row) }` first, else `IndentRegionAt(text, row, tabSize)`. TE4-12's fold commands and TE5's vim folds call it (CANON B20; there is no free `FoldableAt` and no `FoldableEnd`)
  - `std::vector<MarkerFold> ComputeMarkerFolds(std::uint32_t rowCount, const TokenLookup& tokens)`; `bool RefreshMarkerFolds(FoldModel& folds, const HighlightCache& cache, std::uint64_t& seenGeneration)` (Syntax) -- **TE4-12 calls `RefreshMarkerFolds` once per frame per view** (with `TextModel::markerGeneration`)

A marker fold starts on a `foldMarkers.begin` line and ends on the matching `foldMarkers.end` line (nesting by stack; an unmatched end or an unclosed begin makes no fold). Folding a marker region hides `(beginRow, endRow]` -- the end-marker line folds with it, like Visual Studio's `#pragma region` -- so as a `FoldRange` it is `{ headerRow = beginRow, lastRow = endRow }`; indentation folds keep TE1's rule (`IndentRegionAt`). TE1's indentation code is not renamed or touched: `FoldableAt` is a new member beside it. Markers come from the tokenizer (`LineTokens::foldMarker`), so only highlighted rows contribute; `RefreshMarkerFolds` recomputes when the cache's `ContentGeneration()` changes and is a no-op for grammars without `foldMarkers`. A marker fold whose end row no longer lies inside the text (the folds are a frame behind an edit) is ignored by `FoldableAt` until the next refresh.

```cpp
    std::optional<FoldRange> FoldModel::FoldableAt(const Rope& text, std::uint32_t row, std::uint32_t tabSize) const
    {
        if (const std::optional<std::uint32_t> end = MarkerFoldEnd(row); end && *end > row && *end < text.LineCount())
            return FoldRange{ row, *end };   // explicit markers first (spec s4.6)
        return IndentRegionAt(text, row, tabSize);
    }

    void FoldModel::SetMarkerFolds(std::vector<MarkerFold> folds)
    {
        std::sort(folds.begin(), folds.end(), [](const MarkerFold& a, const MarkerFold& b) { return a.beginRow < b.beginRow; });
        m_markerFolds = std::move(folds);
    }

    std::optional<std::uint32_t> FoldModel::MarkerFoldEnd(std::uint32_t row) const
    {
        const auto it = std::lower_bound(m_markerFolds.begin(), m_markerFolds.end(), row,
                                         [](const MarkerFold& f, std::uint32_t r) { return f.beginRow < r; });
        if (it == m_markerFolds.end() || it->beginRow != row) return std::nullopt;
        return it->endRow;
    }
```

```cpp
    // grammar without foldMarkers costs one comparison. TE4-12 calls it once
```

`ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Syntax/FoldMarkers.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/FoldMarkers.hpp"

#include <algorithm>

namespace Arcane::Text
{
    std::vector<MarkerFold> ComputeMarkerFolds(std::uint32_t rowCount, const TokenLookup& tokens)
    {
        std::vector<MarkerFold> out;
        std::vector<std::uint32_t> open;
        for (std::uint32_t row = 0; row < rowCount; ++row)
        {
            const LineTokens* t = tokens(row);
            if (!t) continue;
            if (t->foldMarker == FoldMarker::Begin) open.push_back(row);
            else if (t->foldMarker == FoldMarker::End && !open.empty())
            {
                out.push_back({ open.back(), row });
                open.pop_back();
            }
        }
        std::sort(out.begin(), out.end(), [](const MarkerFold& a, const MarkerFold& b) { return a.beginRow < b.beginRow; });
        return out;
    }

    bool RefreshMarkerFolds(FoldModel& folds, const HighlightCache& cache, std::uint64_t& seenGeneration)
    {
        if (cache.ContentGeneration() == seenGeneration) return false;
        seenGeneration = cache.ContentGeneration();
        const GrammarSnapshot& g = cache.Grammar();
        if (!g || !g->Rules().FoldBegin())
        {
            if (folds.MarkerFolds().empty()) return false;
            folds.SetMarkerFolds({});
            return true;
        }
        folds.SetMarkerFolds(ComputeMarkerFolds(cache.RowCount(), [&cache](std::uint32_t r) { return cache.Peek(r); }));
        return true;
    }
}
```

### Task TE3-20: Scope-test runner and the `// ^^^^ scope` sample format (spec s11.2)

**Files:**
- Create: `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Syntax/ScopeTest.hpp`, `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Syntax/ScopeTest.cpp`
- Create: `ArcaneTests/src/Helpers/TextShippedGrammars.hpp`
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/ScopeTestRunnerTest.cpp`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `GrammarRegistry::Find`, `Scopes()` (TE3-12); `Tokenizer`, `StateTable` (TE3-9..11); `RepoRoot()` (`ArcaneTests/src/Helpers/ConstantScan.hpp:34`)
- Produces:
  - `struct ScopeTestFailure { std::uint32_t fileLine, sourceLine, column; std::string expected, actual, note; }`; `struct ScopeTestResult { std::string grammar; std::size_t assertions; std::vector<ScopeTestFailure> failures; std::string error; bool Passed() const; std::string Report() const; }`
  - `ScopeTestResult RunScopeTest(std::string_view fileText, const GrammarRegistry& registry, MatchScratch& scratch)`
  - test helpers `Arcane::Test::ShippedGrammars()`, `RequireScopeTest(sampleFile)`, `RequireNoGrammarProblems(grammarFile)` (used by TE3-21..29)

**The format (Arcane-native).** A sample lives in `data/Syntaxes/tests/` and is the language's own text with assertion lines interleaved:

```text
#! arcsyntax-test grammar="JSON" marker="//"
  "name": "Arcane",
//^^^^^^ entity.name.key.json
//        ^^^^^^^^ string.quoted.double.json
// <- punctuation.section.json
//   ^ - constant.numeric
```

- Line 1 names the grammar and the assertion **marker**; any line starting with the marker is an assertion, every other line is source. Assertion lines are **removed before tokenizing** -- so the format works for languages without line comments (Plain Text, the Arcane log, Markdown) and an assertion never changes a stateful grammar's state.
- `^` carets assert the scope at their own columns of the **most recent source line** (byte columns; the marker occupies columns `0..len-1`); `<-` asserts column 0.
- The expected scope matches when it equals the run's scope or is a dotted prefix of it (`string.quoted` matches `string.quoted.double.json`); `- scope` negates; `none` asserts "no scope" (scope id 0, the default colour).
- A sample passes only with at least one assertion, no malformed assertion line, and no failure. CRLF checkouts are fine (`\r` is stripped).

```cpp
#pragma once

// Grammar scope tests (spec s11.2): a sample file of the language with
// interleaved assertion lines; see the TE3-20 task text for the format.

#include "TextEditor/Syntax/GrammarRegistry.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/Regex.hpp"

#include <cstdint>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <vector>

namespace Arcane::Text
{
    struct ScopeTestFailure
    {
        std::uint32_t fileLine = 0;     // 1-based line of the assertion in the sample
        std::uint32_t sourceLine = 0;   // 1-based line of the source it asserts on
        std::uint32_t column = 0;       // byte column
        std::string expected;
        std::string actual;
        std::string note;               // "malformed", "column past the end", ...
    };

    struct ScopeTestResult
    {
        std::string grammar;
        std::size_t assertions = 0;
        std::vector<ScopeTestFailure> failures;
        std::string error;
        [[nodiscard]] bool Passed() const noexcept { return error.empty() && failures.empty() && assertions > 0; }
        [[nodiscard]] std::string Report() const;
    };

    [[nodiscard]] ScopeTestResult RunScopeTest(std::string_view fileText, const GrammarRegistry& registry, MatchScratch& scratch);
}
```

`ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Syntax/ScopeTest.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/ScopeTest.hpp"

#include "TextEditor/Syntax/StateTable.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/Tokenizer.hpp"

#include <algorithm>

namespace Arcane::Text
{
    namespace
    {
        std::vector<std::string_view> SplitLines(std::string_view text)
        {
            std::vector<std::string_view> out;
            while (!text.empty())
            {
                const std::size_t nl = text.find('\n');
                std::string_view line = text.substr(0, nl);
                if (!line.empty() && line.back() == '\r') line.remove_suffix(1);
                out.push_back(line);
                if (nl == std::string_view::npos) break;
                text.remove_prefix(nl + 1);
            }
            return out;
        }

        bool Quoted(std::string_view& s, std::string_view key, std::string& value)
        {
            if (!s.starts_with(key)) return false;
            s.remove_prefix(key.size());
            const std::size_t q = s.find('"');
            if (q == std::string_view::npos) return false;
            value = std::string(s.substr(0, q));
            s.remove_prefix(q + 1);
            return true;
        }

        ScopeId ScopeAt(const LineTokens& t, std::uint32_t col)
        {
            const auto it = std::upper_bound(t.runs.begin(), t.runs.end(), col,
                                             [](std::uint32_t c, const TokenRun& r) { return c < r.byteStart; });
            return it == t.runs.begin() ? 0 : std::prev(it)->scope;
        }

        bool Matches(std::string_view expected, ScopeId actualId, const std::string& actual)
        {
            if (expected == "none") return actualId == 0;
            return actual == expected || (actual.size() > expected.size() && actual.starts_with(expected) && actual[expected.size()] == '.');
        }
    }

    std::string ScopeTestResult::Report() const
    {
        std::string out = "grammar \"" + grammar + "\": " + std::to_string(assertions) + " assertions";
        if (!error.empty()) out += "; error: " + error;
        for (const ScopeTestFailure& f : failures)
            out += "\n  sample line " + std::to_string(f.fileLine) + " (source line " + std::to_string(f.sourceLine) + ", col " +
                   std::to_string(f.column) + "): expected " + f.expected + ", got " + (f.actual.empty() ? "none" : f.actual) +
                   (f.note.empty() ? "" : " [" + f.note + "]");
        return out;
    }

    ScopeTestResult RunScopeTest(std::string_view fileText, const GrammarRegistry& registry, MatchScratch& scratch)
    {
        ScopeTestResult out;
        const std::vector<std::string_view> lines = SplitLines(fileText);
        std::string marker;
        {
            std::string_view head = lines.empty() ? std::string_view() : lines[0];
            if (!Quoted(head, "#! arcsyntax-test grammar=\"", out.grammar) || !Quoted(head, " marker=\"", marker) || marker.empty())
            {
                out.error = "line 1 must be: #! arcsyntax-test grammar=\"<name>\" marker=\"<marker>\"";
                return out;
            }
        }
        const GrammarSnapshot g = registry.Find(out.grammar);
        if (!g)
        {
            out.error = "grammar \"" + out.grammar + "\" is not loaded";
            return out;
        }
        StateTable states;
        Tokenizer tokenizer(*g, states, scratch);
        LineTokens tokens;
        std::string_view source;
        bool haveSource = false;
        std::uint32_t sourceLine = 0;
        StateId state = StateTable::kRoot;

        for (std::size_t i = 1; i < lines.size(); ++i)
        {
            const auto fileLine = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(i + 1);
            const std::string_view l = lines[i];
            if (!l.starts_with(marker))
            {
                source = l;
                haveSource = true;
                sourceLine = fileLine;
                tokens = tokenizer.TokenizeLine(source, state);
                state = tokens.endState;
                continue;
            }
            std::string_view rest = l.substr(marker.size());
            const std::size_t spaces = rest.find_first_not_of(' ');
            const auto malformed = [&](std::string note) {
                out.failures.push_back({ fileLine, sourceLine, 0, "<assertion>", std::string(l), std::move(note) });
            };
            if (spaces == std::string_view::npos) { malformed("malformed"); continue; }
            rest.remove_prefix(spaces);
            std::uint32_t firstCol = 0, count = 0;
            if (rest.starts_with("<-"))
            {
                count = 1;
                rest.remove_prefix(2);
            }
            else
            {
                const std::size_t carets = rest.find_first_not_of('^');
                count = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(carets == std::string_view::npos ? rest.size() : carets);
                if (count == 0) { malformed("malformed"); continue; }
                firstCol = static_cast<std::uint32_t>(marker.size() + spaces);
                rest.remove_prefix(count);
            }
            if (rest.empty() || rest.front() != ' ') { malformed("malformed: a space must separate the marks from the scope"); continue; }
            rest.remove_prefix(rest.find_first_not_of(' ') == std::string_view::npos ? rest.size() : rest.find_first_not_of(' '));
            bool negate = false;
            if (rest.starts_with("- "))
            {
                negate = true;
                rest.remove_prefix(2);
                rest.remove_prefix(std::min(rest.size(), rest.find_first_not_of(' ')));
            }
            const std::size_t scopeEnd = rest.find(' ');
            const std::string expected(rest.substr(0, scopeEnd));
            if (expected.empty() || (scopeEnd != std::string_view::npos && rest.find_first_not_of(' ', scopeEnd) != std::string_view::npos))
            {
                malformed("malformed");
                continue;
            }
            if (!haveSource)
            {
                out.failures.push_back({ fileLine, 0, firstCol, expected, {}, "assertion before any source line" });
                continue;
            }
            for (std::uint32_t c = firstCol; c < firstCol + count; ++c)
            {
                ++out.assertions;
                if (c >= source.size())
                {
                    out.failures.push_back({ fileLine, sourceLine, c, expected, {}, "column past the end of the source line" });
                    continue;
                }
                const ScopeId id = ScopeAt(tokens, c);
                const std::string actual = registry.Scopes().Name(id);
                if (Matches(expected, id, actual) == negate)
                    out.failures.push_back({ fileLine, sourceLine, c, (negate ? "- " : "") + expected, actual, {} });
            }
        }
        if (out.assertions == 0 && out.error.empty()) out.error = "the sample has no assertions";
        return out;
    }
}
```

`ArcaneTests/src/Helpers/TextShippedGrammars.hpp`:

```cpp
#pragma once

// The repo's data/Syntaxes grammars, loaded once per test run, and the
// per-grammar checks every grammar task uses (spec s4.7, s11.2).

#include "Helpers/ConstantScan.hpp"   // RepoRoot()
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/GrammarRegistry.hpp"
#include "TextEditor/Syntax/ScopeTest.hpp"

#include <catch2/catch_test_macros.hpp>

#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <iterator>
#include <map>
#include <string>

namespace Arcane::Test
{
    struct ShippedGrammarSet
    {
        Arcane::Text::GrammarRegistry registry;
        std::map<std::string, std::vector<Arcane::Text::GrammarProblem>> problems;
        ShippedGrammarSet()
        {
            registry.SetProblemSink([this](std::string_view key, std::span<const Arcane::Text::GrammarProblem> rows) {
                if (rows.empty()) problems.erase(std::string(key));
                else problems[std::string(key)].assign(rows.begin(), rows.end());
            });
            registry.SetSearchDirs({ { RepoRoot() / "data" / "Syntaxes", Arcane::Text::GrammarOrigin::Engine } });
            registry.Reload();
        }
    };

    inline ShippedGrammarSet& ShippedGrammars()
    {
        static ShippedGrammarSet set;
        return set;
    }

    inline void RequireScopeTest(std::string_view sampleFile)
    {
        const std::filesystem::path path = RepoRoot() / "data" / "Syntaxes" / "tests" / std::string(sampleFile);
        std::ifstream in(path, std::ios::binary);
        INFO(path.generic_string());
        REQUIRE(in.good());
        const std::string text((std::istreambuf_iterator<char>(in)), std::istreambuf_iterator<char>());
        Arcane::Text::MatchScratch scratch{ Arcane::Text::RegexLimits{} };
        const Arcane::Text::ScopeTestResult r = Arcane::Text::RunScopeTest(text, ShippedGrammars().registry, scratch);
        INFO(r.Report());
        CHECK(r.Passed());
    }

    inline void RequireNoGrammarProblems(std::string_view grammarFile)
    {
        const std::string key = "text.grammar:" + (RepoRoot() / "data" / "Syntaxes" / std::string(grammarFile)).generic_string();
        const auto& p = ShippedGrammars().problems;
        INFO(key);
        CHECK(ShippedGrammars().registry.Names().size() > 1u);   // the directory held at least one grammar
        if (const auto it = p.find(key); it != p.end())
            for (const auto& row : it->second)
            {
                INFO(row.rulePath + ": " + row.message);
                CHECK(false);
            }
    }
}
```

**Files:**

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `RequireScopeTest`, `RequireNoGrammarProblems`, `ShippedGrammars` (TE3-20); `GrammarRegistry::Detect`, `Find` (TE3-12)
- Produces: the grammar `"JSON"` in the engine search directory

The spec's s4.1 example, completed: the key rule is a single-line `match` with a lookahead, listed **before** the string region so it wins the tie at the same position (s4.1, "context-dependent scopes use ordinary rules"). Arcane's JSON assets are listed by extension: `.arcmat .arcproj .arcscene .arctheme .arcsyntax .arcmesh .arcsprite .arcinput .arcdiag .arcplugin .meta` (every JSON-backed extension in the engine and ReferenceProject; `.arcart` is a binary artifact and is not listed). `//` and `/* */` comments are accepted (JSONC), which is also what lets the sample carry `//` assertion lines; an escape inside a string is coloured by a nested rule, an invalid escape is `invalid.illegal`.

### Task TE3-22: Plain Text and INI/cfg (line-local) grammars (spec s4.1, s4.7)

**Files:**
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/PlainText.arcsyntax`, `data/Syntaxes/INI.arcsyntax`
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_plaintext.txt`, `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_ini.ini`
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/GrammarScopeTests.cpp` (one case appended)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `RequireScopeTest`, `RequireNoGrammarProblems`, `ShippedGrammars` (TE3-20); `GrammarRegistry::Detect`, `Find` (TE3-12)
- Produces: the grammars `"Plain Text"`, `"INI"` in the engine search directory

`PlainText.arcsyntax` is the data-file form of the built-in fallback (TE3-8's `MakePlainTextGrammar`; a valid file replaces it, TE3-12): line-local, no rules, `.txt`/`.text`. INI is **line-local** (s4.1): every line starts at the root and a quote left open at the end of a line is force-closed there -- the sample's `title = "Arcane \"Editor\"` line leaves its string open and the next line's key still colours as a key. Comments are `;` or `#` at line start, or after whitespace; sections, `key = value` / `key: value`, quoted strings, booleans (`true/false/yes/no/on/off`, any case) and numbers.

```json
    { "match": "^\\s*([^=:;#\\s\\[][^=:]*?)\\s*([=:])",
      "captures": { "1": "entity.name.key.ini", "2": "punctuation.separator.key-value.ini" } },
```

### Task TE3-23: Arcane log grammar (line-local; Console level colours) (spec s4.1, s4.4, s4.7)

**Files:**
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/ArcaneLog.arcsyntax`
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_arcanelog.log`
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/GrammarScopeTests.cpp` (one case appended)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `RequireScopeTest`, `RequireNoGrammarProblems`, `ShippedGrammars` (TE3-20); `GrammarRegistry::Detect`, `Find` (TE3-12)
- Produces: the grammar `"Arcane Log"` in the engine search directory

The line format is the engine logger's (`ArcaneCore/src/Arcane/Base/Log.cpp:236`, `Util/LogServerSettingsData.hpp:25-26`): file sinks write `[%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%e] [%n] [%l] %v` (e.g. `[2026-10-06 03:34:40.538] [Arcane] [warning] ...`), the console pattern `[%H:%M:%S.%e] [%n] [%l] %v`; spdlog's `%l` names are `trace debug info warning error critical`; messages often start with `[tag]` (`[nri]`, `[nri-graph]`, `[foreign-module]`). Scopes: `constant.other.timestamp.log`, `entity.name.logger.log`, `markup.log.level.<level>.log` on the `[level]` token and `markup.log.message.<level>.log` on the rest of the line (a region from the level to the end of the line -- line-local force-close keeps it to that line), `entity.name.tag.log` on message tags. The Dark/Light/built-in syntax colours (TE3-6) map warning/error/critical to the palette's `warning`/`error` tokens -- the colours the Console uses (`Panels/EditorPanels.cpp:1269-1270`). Lines without the header (stack frames, continuation lines) are plain. Line-local, so a 400 MB log stays coloured at any scroll position (s4.4).

```cpp
TEST_CASE("Grammar HLSL: loads clean, passes its scope test, marks #pragma region folds", "[text-grammar-hlsl][text-syntax-data]")
{
    RequireNoGrammarProblems("HLSL.arcsyntax");
    RequireScopeTest("syntax_test_hlsl.hlsl");

    for (const char* f : { "a.hlsl", "b.hlsli", "c.fx" }) CHECK(reg.Detect(f, "", {})->Name() == "HLSL");
    REQUIRE(reg.Find("HLSL") != nullptr);
    REQUIRE(reg.Find("HLSL")->Rules().FoldBegin() != nullptr);
    Arcane::Text::StateTable states;
    Arcane::Text::MatchScratch scratch{ Arcane::Text::RegexLimits{} };
    Arcane::Text::Tokenizer t(*reg.Find("HLSL"), states, scratch);
    CHECK(t.TokenizeLine("#pragma region Lighting", Arcane::Text::StateTable::kRoot).foldMarker == Arcane::Text::FoldMarker::Begin);
    CHECK(t.TokenizeLine("  #pragma endregion", Arcane::Text::StateTable::kRoot).foldMarker == Arcane::Text::FoldMarker::End);
}
```

### Task TE3-25: Lua grammar, ported from lite-xl (MIT) (spec s4.7, s10)

**Files:**
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/Lua.arcsyntax`
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_lua.lua`
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/NOTICE-lite-xl.txt` (lite-xl's `LICENSE`, verbatim)
- Modify: `NOTICE.md` (after the "Reimplemented (not vendored)" list: a "Ported grammar content" entry)
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/GrammarScopeTests.cpp` (one case appended)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `RequireScopeTest`, `RequireNoGrammarProblems`, `ShippedGrammars` (TE3-20); `GrammarRegistry::Detect`, `Find` (TE3-12)
- Produces: the grammar `"Lua"` in the engine search directory

Translated from lite-xl's `data/plugins/language_lua.lua` (`D:\dev\_reference\lite-xl-master`, MIT; the spec's s4.7 instruction): lite-xl's Lua patterns become PCRE2 (`%a`->`[A-Za-z]`, `%w`->`[A-Za-z0-9]`, `%d`->`[0-9]`, the `%f[...]` frontier for call names -> a `(?=\s*[("'{])` lookahead, `{ start, end, escape }` triples -> `begin`/`end`/`escape` regions), and its `symbols` table becomes the identifier rules' `keywords` (split into control / logical-operator / storage / `self` / literal scopes instead of lite-xl's two "keyword" kinds). Additions over the original: long-bracket strings and comments with one and two `=` levels (`[=[ ]=]`, `--[==[ ]==]`; lite-xl only has level 0), escape colouring inside strings, `::label::`. Covers premake scripts (`.lua`). The attribution is in the file's `"notice"` field, the full MIT text in `data/Syntaxes/NOTICE-lite-xl.txt`, and a `NOTICE.md` entry.

```json
{
  "format": "arcsyntax",
  "version": 1,
  "name": "Lua",
  "scope": "source.lua",
  "notice": "Rules translated from lite-xl data/plugins/language_lua.lua (MIT License; Copyright (c) 2020 rxi, 2020-2022 Francesco Abbate, 2022-present Lite XL Team). See NOTICE.md.",
  "files": [".lua", ".rockspec"],
  "firstLine": "^#!.*[ /]lua",
  "comment": { "line": "--", "block": ["--[[", "]]"] },
  "brackets": [["(", ")"], ["[", "]"], ["{", "}"]],
  "autoClose": [["\"", "\""], ["'", "'"], ["(", ")"], ["[", "]"], ["{", "}"]],
  "indent": { "increase": "^\\s*(?:(?:local\\s+)?function\\b|.*\\b(?:then|do|repeat)\\s*(?:--.*)?$|.*[{(]\\s*(?:--.*)?$)",
              "decrease": "^\\s*(?:end\\b|else\\b|elseif\\b|until\\b|[})\\]])" },
  "wordChars": "A-Za-z0-9_",

  "lineLocal": false,
  "patterns": [
    { "begin": "--\\[\\[", "end": "\\]\\]", "scope": "comment.block.lua" },
    { "begin": "--\\[=\\[", "end": "\\]=\\]", "scope": "comment.block.lua" },
    { "begin": "--\\[==\\[", "end": "\\]==\\]", "scope": "comment.block.lua" },
    { "match": "--.*$", "scope": "comment.line.double-dash.lua" },
    { "begin": "\\[\\[", "end": "\\]\\]", "scope": "string.quoted.other.multiline.lua" },
    { "begin": "\\[=\\[", "end": "\\]=\\]", "scope": "string.quoted.other.multiline.lua" },
    { "begin": "\\[==\\[", "end": "\\]==\\]", "scope": "string.quoted.other.multiline.lua" },

    { "begin": "'", "end": "'", "escape": "\\\\.", "scope": "string.quoted.single.lua",

    { "match": "(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])0[xX](?:[0-9A-Fa-f]+(?:\\.[0-9A-Fa-f]*)?|\\.[0-9A-Fa-f]+)(?:[pP][-+]?[0-9]+)?",

    { "match": "<(?:const|close)>", "scope": "storage.modifier.attribute.lua" },
    { "match": "\\.\\.\\.?|[<>~=]=|//|[-+*/%^#<>=]", "scope": "keyword.operator.lua" },
```

### Task TE3-26: TOML and YAML grammars (spec s4.7)

**Files:**
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/TOML.arcsyntax`, `data/Syntaxes/YAML.arcsyntax`
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_toml.toml`, `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_yaml.yaml`
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/GrammarScopeTests.cpp` (one case appended)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `RequireScopeTest`, `RequireNoGrammarProblems`, `ShippedGrammars` (TE3-20); `GrammarRegistry::Detect`, `Find` (TE3-12)
- Produces: the grammars `"TOML"`, `"YAML"` in the engine search directory

Both written fresh. TOML: comments, `[table]` / `[[array of tables]]` headers, bare/quoted/dotted keys (a key is whatever precedes `=`, by lookahead), the four string forms (basic and literal, single- and triple-quoted; triple-quoted ones span lines), escapes, offset date-times, numbers (hex/octal/binary, `_` separators, `inf`/`nan`), booleans. YAML: comments (`#` at line start or after whitespace), document markers, `%` directives, list dashes, keys (plain or quoted, before `: `), anchors/aliases, tags, block-scalar indicators, double-quoted strings with escapes, single-quoted strings with `''`, the YAML 1.1 boolean/null spellings, numbers (not when glued to `:`/`/`, so `host:8080/x` stays plain). Known limit: a block scalar's content lines are not distinguished from plain text (it needs indentation tracking, which a pattern grammar cannot do); they draw as plain scalars.

`data/Syntaxes/TOML.arcsyntax`:

```json
{
  "format": "arcsyntax",
  "version": 1,
  "name": "TOML",
  "scope": "source.toml",
  "files": [".toml"],
  "comment": { "line": "#" },
  "brackets": [["[", "]"], ["{", "}"]],
  "autoClose": [["\"", "\""], ["'", "'"], ["[", "]"], ["{", "}"]],
  "indent": { "increase": "[\\[{]\\s*$", "decrease": "^\\s*[\\]}]" },
  "wordChars": "A-Za-z0-9_-",
  "symbols": [ { "match": "^\\s*\\[\\[?\\s*([^\\]]+?)\\s*\\]\\]?", "name": 1, "kind": "table" } ],
  "lineLocal": false,
  "patterns": [
    { "match": "#.*$", "scope": "comment.line.number-sign.toml" },
    { "match": "^\\s*(\\[\\[?)([^\\]]*)(\\]\\]?)",
      "captures": { "1": "punctuation.definition.table.toml", "2": "entity.name.section.toml", "3": "punctuation.definition.table.toml" } },
    { "match": "(?:[A-Za-z0-9_-]+|\"(?:[^\"\\\\]|\\\\.)*\"|'[^']*')(?:\\s*\\.\\s*(?:[A-Za-z0-9_-]+|\"(?:[^\"\\\\]|\\\\.)*\"|'[^']*'))*(?=\\s*=)",
      "scope": "entity.name.key.toml" },
    { "begin": "\"\"\"", "end": "\"\"\"(?!\")", "escape": "\\\\.", "scope": "string.quoted.triple.basic.toml",
      "patterns": [ { "match": "\\\\(?:[btnfr\"\\\\]|u[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}|U[0-9A-Fa-f]{8})", "scope": "constant.character.escape.toml" } ] },
    { "begin": "'''", "end": "'''(?!')", "scope": "string.quoted.triple.literal.toml" },
    { "begin": "\"", "end": "\"", "escape": "\\\\.", "scope": "string.quoted.double.basic.toml",
      "patterns": [ { "match": "\\\\(?:[btnfr\"\\\\]|u[0-9A-Fa-f]{4}|U[0-9A-Fa-f]{8})", "scope": "constant.character.escape.toml" } ] },
    { "begin": "'", "end": "'", "scope": "string.quoted.single.literal.toml" },
    { "match": "\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}(?:[Tt ]\\d{2}:\\d{2}:\\d{2}(?:\\.\\d+)?(?:[Zz]|[+-]\\d{2}:\\d{2})?)?|\\d{2}:\\d{2}:\\d{2}(?:\\.\\d+)?",
      "scope": "constant.other.datetime.toml" },
    { "match": "(?<![\\w.-])(?:true|false)(?![\\w.-])", "scope": "constant.language.boolean.toml" },
    { "match": "(?<![\\w.-])[+-]?(?:0x[0-9A-Fa-f_]+|0o[0-7_]+|0b[01_]+|inf|nan|[0-9][0-9_]*(?:\\.[0-9][0-9_]*)?(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9][0-9_]*)?)(?![\\w.-])",
      "scope": "constant.numeric.toml" },
    { "match": "=", "scope": "keyword.operator.assignment.toml" },
    { "match": "[\\[\\]{},]", "scope": "punctuation.section.toml" }
  ]
}
```

### Task TE3-27: XML grammar (spec s4.7)

**Files:**
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/XML.arcsyntax`
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_xml.xml`
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/GrammarScopeTests.cpp` (one case appended)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `RequireScopeTest`, `RequireNoGrammarProblems`, `ShippedGrammars` (TE3-20); `GrammarRegistry::Detect`, `Find` (TE3-12)
- Produces: the grammar `"XML"` in the engine search directory

Written fresh. Comments, CDATA, processing instructions (`<?xml ...?>`), `<!DOCTYPE ...>`, and tags as a region from `<`/`</` to `>`/`/>` whose nested rules colour the tag name (by lookbehind on `<` / `</` -- no `\G` needed), attribute names, `=`, quoted values with entity references; entities in text. `brackets` is `< >` so the matcher pairs tags' angle brackets. Files include the Visual Studio/MSBuild family (`.vcxproj .props .targets .filters .slnx .natvis`) that Arcane projects contain.

### Task TE3-28: Batch, PowerShell and shell grammars (spec s4.7)

**Files:**
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/Batch.arcsyntax`, `data/Syntaxes/PowerShell.arcsyntax`, `data/Syntaxes/Shell.arcsyntax`
- Create: `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_batch.bat`, `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_powershell.ps1`, `data/Syntaxes/tests/syntax_test_shell.sh`
- Test: `ArcaneTests/src/Text/GrammarScopeTests.cpp` (one case appended)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `RequireScopeTest`, `RequireNoGrammarProblems`, `ShippedGrammars` (TE3-20); `GrammarRegistry::Detect`, `Find` (TE3-12)
- Produces: the grammars `"Batch"`, `"PowerShell"`, `"Shell"` in the engine search directory

All three written fresh. **Batch** is line-local (cmd parses line by line): `REM`/`::` comments, labels, `%var%`/`%%f`/`%~1`/`!delayed!` variables (also inside strings), control keywords and builtin commands (case-insensitive, via `(?i)` -- keyword tables are exact-match), `@`, redirection/pipe operators, numbers. **PowerShell** (stateful): `<# #>` block and `#` line comments, here-strings (`@"`...`"@`, `@'`...`'@`), double-quoted strings with backtick escapes and `$variable` interpolation, single-quoted strings with `''`, `$true/$false/$null`, variables (scoped `$env:X`, `${...}`), `-eq`-style operators, `Verb-Noun` cmdlets, `[type]` literals, `-Parameter` names, numbers with `KB/MB/...` suffixes, control keywords (case-insensitive). **Shell** (stateful): shebang, `#` comments (only at a word start), double-quoted strings with escapes and `$var`/`${...}` interpolation, single-quoted strings, `$(`/`$((`/backtick substitution openers, heredoc operators, control keywords, `local/export/...`, builtins, assignments (`NAME=`), operators, numbers. Known limit: a heredoc's body is not recognised (its terminator is a back-reference across lines, which `.arcsyntax` regions cannot express).

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `RequireScopeTest`, `RequireNoGrammarProblems`, `ShippedGrammars` (TE3-20); `GrammarRegistry::Detect`, `Find` (TE3-12)
- Produces: the grammar `"Markdown"` in the engine search directory

Translated from lite-xl's `data/plugins/language_md.lua` (MIT): headings, thematic breaks (lite-xl colours them as comments; here `meta.separator`), bullets and numbered lists, block quotes, reference definitions, inline code (single and double backticks), bold/italic/bold-italic with `*` and `_` (underscore emphasis only at word boundaries, so `snake_case_name` stays plain), strikethrough, links and images, reference links, autolinks and bare URLs, inline HTML tags and entities, HTML comments, emoji shortcodes, `$$` math. lite-xl's fence list (40+ languages via `syntax = ".ext"`) becomes **`embed`** regions (s4.1) for the v1 grammars only -- `json/jsonc`, `hlsl`, `lua`, `xml/html/svg`, `yaml/yml`, `toml`, `ini/cfg`, `sh/bash/shell/zsh`, `powershell/ps1/pwsh`, `bat/batch/cmd`, `log` -- plus a generic fence drawn as `markup.raw.block`. The fence's `end` is an embed **boundary** (TE3-10): an unterminated string inside fenced JSON still ends at the closing fence. Single-line emphasis only (lite-xl's multi-line emphasis regions would colour the rest of a document after one stray `*`). Because it embeds every other grammar, this task is last; its test also asserts the whole shipped set loads with zero Problems rows.

```cpp
TEST_CASE("Grammar Markdown: loads clean, passes its scope test (with embedded JSON and Lua), resolves every embed", "[text-grammar-markdown][text-syntax-data]")
{
    RequireNoGrammarProblems("Markdown.arcsyntax");
    RequireScopeTest("syntax_test_markdown.md");
    auto& reg = ShippedGrammars().registry;
    CHECK(reg.Detect("README.md", "", {})->Name() == "Markdown");
    const auto md = reg.Find("Markdown");
    REQUIRE(md != nullptr);
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < md->Embeds().size(); ++i)
    {
        INFO(md->Rules().EmbedNames()[i]);
        CHECK(md->Embeds()[i] != nullptr);   // every fence language is a shipped grammar
    }
    CHECK(md->Rules().Desc().notice.find("lite-xl") != std::string::npos);
}
```

**Files:**

- Modify (TE2's files): `ArcaneEditor/src/TextEditor/Document/TextDocument.hpp/.cpp` (`TextDocumentServices::syntax`; the document owns its `HighlightCache`, installs the view's colour runs through `View().SetRowColorRuns`, updates the cache once per frame). `TextEditorView` is NOT modified (CANON A7: TE2-13's `SetRowColorRuns` seam replaces the old `DrawRow`/`RowLayout::XAt` assumption)
